title: Leaving the Howard for the Standard Theater in Philadelphia
summary: He and Sandy Williams went to Philadelphia to work for Gibson at the Standard Theater under the Nicholas brothers' father, with their mother on piano.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, so you stayed at the Howard for about four years?
Yeah, three or four years. Uh-huh.
And after you left the club, were you doing any other work on the side, or was it principally at the Howard?

At the Howard, and when I left the Howard I came to Philadelphia and to the Standard Theater. And we worked in there for Gibson, worked in his theater there for about three years, maybe, or something like that, and that was a very good job. Sandy Williams and I, we were --
Both again?
Yeah, we were -- we came -- we left the Howard and we came to Philadelphia together.
Why did you go to Philadelphia?
Well, they needed a band there. They needed some musicians, and the pay was good, sounded good, so we (finger snap) picked up there.
Were you the leader of the band in Philadelphia?
No. The Nicholas father -- Nicholas brothers' father was the leader.
I'll be darned. What was his first name?
He used to be called Nick for short. I don't know his --
Well, that's sort of hard to figure. (Inaudible.)
(Inaudible.)
Yeah, what was his name?
They always do.
What's the Nicholas brothers' father? Fayette and what's-his-name were the two boys. I saw them grow from here, from there, and the wife played piano.
Oh, really?
Uh-huh, Mrs. Nicholas.
The whole family act there.
Uh-huh.
